title: Building a RAG-based chat bot agent
short: Being able to retrieve data from documents with AI is plausible now.
body:
In this project we have used different tools, models and frameworks to build a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot agent. It connects a standard AI model to specific, external data sources—like company documents, FAQs, or live databases.

Motivation

In today’s data-driven environment, having quick and reliable access to essential documents is increasingly important. Corporations and individuals often work with large and complex collections of information that can be time-consuming to review and analyze. Thanks to recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI frameworks, RAG systems can help address this challenge by enabling users to efficiently search, understand, and interact with their documents. For example, a RAG-based system can analyze emails, answer questions about legal textbooks, or provide insights from chemistry lecture notes.

Method

We used LangChain and the OpenAI API to develop the chatbot agent. The system retrieves and stores document data in a vector database, then uses cosine similarity to identify the vectors that are most relevant to a user's query. A user interface was also developed to provide an accessible way to interact with the chatbot. We deployed this interface as a pilot version, allowing each user to ask up to five questions before contacting an administrator for further access. Users can view their chat history, upload new documents, and remove existing documents. Authentication is also an essential component of the system, ensuring that only authorized users can access the chatbot agent
